claims.cards/front_squat.json#c3: In a correct rack the shoulders hold the bar, pushed forward and slightly up (a shrug makes a shelf for it); the hands and arms only add security and should not do the main work, and a fingertip rack is fine if the bar stays on the shoulders.
claims.cards/front_squat.json#c4: Keep the hands wrapped round the bar as far as possible with a loose grip, elbows high, bar supported on the trunk.
claims.cards/front_squat.json#c7: Keep the elbows high, or the bar may slip; the lift trains a tall chest and stops the habit of leaning forward.
claims.cards/goblet_squat.json#g1: Stand with feet hip width and hold a kettlebell or dumbbell upright at chest height, both hands cupping the top of the weight.
claims.cards/goblet_squat.json#g2: Feet about shoulder width, dumbbell upright in front of the chest, elbows close to the ribs and back straight while lowering.
claims.cards/goblet_squat.json#g5: Keep the weight secure at chest height for the whole rep.
claims.cards/goblet_squat.json#g6: Common mistakes: leaning too far forward (more lower-back strain), and the chest drooping or the weight drifting away from the body.
claims.cards/mountain_climbers.json#c6: Shifting the weight backward makes balance harder; keep the shoulders over the wrists and press slightly forward.
claims.shared/front-rack-exemption.json#c1: In a correct clean rack the shoulders hold the bar; the hands and arms only add security and should not do the main work of holding it.
claims.shared/front-rack-exemption.json#c4: A fingertip rack with the bar supported by the shoulders is better than a full grip with the bar not fully supported by the shoulders.
claims.shared/front-rack-exemption.json#c5: For the front squat: bar in the channel between the throat and the top of the shoulders, hands wrapped round the bar as much as possible with the elbows high and the bar supported on the trunk, but the grip loose.
claims.shared/implement-battle-ropes.json#c1: Hold one rope end in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
claims.shared/implement-battle-ropes.json#c3: The rope lies in the palm, the fingers wrap around it and the thumb closes over the fingers, on top.
claims.shared/implement-battle-ropes.json#c4: Grip firmly but relaxed; gripping too tightly tires the forearms.
claims.shared/implement-jump-rope.json#c2: The handles are gripped with the thumb and index fingers.
claims.shared/implement-kettlebell-swing.json#c: One kettlebell school rejects swinging with the thumbs up (hammer grip), saying that moving the bell fast that way risks the elbows at the bottom of the backswing; the article is mainly about cleans and one-arm and double work, so for the two-hand swing this is inference.
claims.shared/implement-wall-ball.json#c1: Catch the ball with the hands underneath it rather than on its sides.
claims.shared/implement-wall-ball.json#c2: Keep the elbows high in front of you, not out to the sides.
claims.shared/implement-wall-ball.json#c3: Catch the ball close to the body with the wrists about six inches apart.
claims.shared/implement-wall-ball.json#c4: Catching the ball on its sides can let it fall out of the hands.
claims.shared/palm-flat.json#c1: In the push-up the palms are flat, hands shoulder-width, fingers facing forward or turned slightly inward, with the shoulders directly over the hands.
claims.shared/palm-flat.json#c2: Hands should face forward, not angled, with every part of the hand and fingers on the floor; cupping the palm or lifting the fingers puts all the pressure on the heel of the hand and leads to wrist discomfort.
claims.shared/palm-flat.json#c3: Hands wide and far in front of the chest, relaxed hands, or hands rotated to one side strain the wrist; at the top of the push-up the hands sit directly under the shoulders, and hands in front of or behind the shoulders increase wrist pressure.
claims.shared/palm-flat.json#c5: One coaching source says pushing through the heel and outside surface of the palm gives more force and steadier shoulders.
claims.shared/palm-flat.json#c6: On hands and knees (bird dog) the hands go directly under the shoulders, shoulder-width, fingers facing forward; at the bottom of a push-up the forearms sit on top of the wrists in a straight line.
